analysis.title: Macro & Markets Forecast Edition - December: hikes still in view for the Fed and ECB
key_insights: Nordea keeps its Fed call unchanged: a 25bp hike in December and one more hike in 2027. Recent data show the US economy still running hot.

US data since the last update: October payrolls +165,000 (more than double expected), unemployment 4.1%, average hourly earnings +0.4% on the month, core CPI +0.3% in October (above expectations, third such increase in a row), core PCE 3.1% in September.

The Fed held at 3.75-4.00% in October with two dissents in favor of a hike. Governor Waller favors a 25bp hike in December and said a 50bp move should be considered if inflation stays this strong; he warned a 25bp hike alone would put Fed credibility at risk.

Price pressures are broad. ISM prices paid were 75.2 in manufacturing and 73.0 in services in October, both above 70 for most of the year, and service firms say they have not yet passed on all higher costs.

Demand is strong: the AI buildout keeps investment high and rising stock prices have lifted household wealth and consumer spending. Unemployment has been between 4.1% and 4.3% since March. Nordea says policy may not yet be tight enough.

Upside risk to the Fed path: monthly core increases of about 0.3% imply roughly 3.6% annualized inflation, with supercore running near that pace. Markets price about a 12% chance of a 50bp hike in December.

Downside risk from an AI setback: the Nasdaq fell over 5% last Thursday, its worst day since April 2025, on chip and data center worries. The four largest US hyperscalers are expected to invest more than $1 trillion next year, and Nordea questions whether AI demand will grow enough to justify it.

Nordea expects the direct economic hit from an AI investment disappointment to be meaningful but limited: tech employment has already weakened and AI spending has a high import share. The larger channel is household wealth, which rose $12.8 trillion in Q2 and is at a record relative to income, with the saving rate at 3.8% in September, the lowest since 2022.

In an AI downturn, short-term rates would fall but by less than in the dot-com bust (6.5% to 1.75% in 2001, 1% by mid-2003), since inflation is already high and the Fed has less room to cut. The long end may be more resilient: the 5y5y forward fell only about 2 points in the dot-com episode.

Government borrowing (deficit near $2 trillion, about 6% of GDP, last fiscal year) and a higher term premium could put a floor under long-term yields, so tech stocks could fall sharply without long yields following. The recent Nasdaq-yield relationship may not hold.

The AI downturn is not a near-term risk to the Fed call because investment would have to slow first, then jobs and wealth, then consumption. Nordea is confident in a December hike and one more next year, with the path beyond very uncertain.
ECB: Nordea still expects a 25bp hike in December and another in March 2027, taking the deposit rate to 3%. Chief Economist Lane said it would be prudent to hike again unless incoming data change.

The ECB's October message turned less hawkish, noting high energy prices as downside risk to growth and upside risk to inflation. Headline inflation is double the 2% target while core is unchanged at 2.5%, so the ECB can proceed at a quarterly pace. Risks have shifted slightly to the downside and the ECB could pause earlier than Nordea's baseline.

Longer bond yields have corrected lower after a climb during summer and early autumn. Nordea still sees medium-term upward pressure via higher bond risk premia, with a weaker cyclical outlook as the main downside risk to that view.

sector_views.rationale: Nordea sees the AI investment case as questionable and a sharp fall in tech stocks as a risk, but not a near-term threat to its Fed call.

risk_factors: Sticky US inflation could force the Fed to hike more than 25bp in December or more than two times in total.
An AI investment setback could hit tech stocks, household wealth and consumption, and weigh most on short-term rates.
Uncertain AI demand: costly model operation, fierce competition, easy provider switching and free open-weight models only months behind paid ones.
Weaker euro area growth, tighter financing conditions and absent broadening of price pressures could lead the ECB to pause earlier.
A reversal of the recent drop in energy prices could keep inflation high in the euro area.
A weaker cyclical outlook could push bond yields lower, against Nordea's higher-yield view.

tension_points.bull_case: Hot data (payrolls +165,000, core CPI +0.3% three months running, ISM prices paid above 70) support a December hike and one more in 2027, with Waller open to 50bp.
tension_points.bear_case: An AI investment setback could hit stocks and household wealth, cut consumption and pull rates lower, mainly at the short end.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Not a near-term risk. It would require investment to slow first, then spread to jobs and household wealth, then to consumption.

tension_points.bull_case: Headline inflation is double target and Lane said a December hike is prudent unless data change, supporting 25bp in December and March 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Weaker growth data, tighter financing conditions and no broadening of price pressures could lead the ECB to pause earlier.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Incoming data changing before the December meeting, per Lane.
